test_title: PYST 36: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Pick the INCORRECT statement regarding the life of Birsa Munda.

options.text: He urged people to destroy the Europeans.
He advised his people to bring back the Golden Age of Mundas.
Birsa was born in the forests of Madhya Pradesh.
He had joined the local missionary school.

solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Birsa was born in the forests of Madhya Pradesh.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Birsa Munda** was born on **15 November 1875** in the village of **Ulihatu**, which is located in the current **Jharkhand** state, not in Madhya Pradesh. Hence, the statement "Birsa was born in the forests of Madhya Pradesh" is incorrect.
 
• He urged his people to **destroy the European influence** and their exploitative practices, which were adversely affecting the tribal communities. This statement is **correct**.
 
• Birsa Munda inspired his followers to bring back the **Golden Age of the Munda community**, emphasizing traditional tribal values and the rejection of British and missionary influence. This statement is also **correct**.
 
• Birsa Munda received his early education at a **local missionary school**, where he was introduced to Christianity. However, he later rejected Christianity and returned to his traditional tribal roots. This statement is **correct**.
 
• His role as a tribal leader and his rebellion against the British earned him the title of **‘Dharti Abba’** (Father of the Earth).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Birsa Munda and the Tribal Movement:**

 
 
• Birsa Munda led the **Ulgulan (The Great Rebellion)** against the British in the late 19th century, which was one of the most significant tribal uprisings in colonial India.
 
• He fought against the exploitation of tribal lands by the British and moneylenders, opposing the **‘Zamindari’ system**.
 
• His movement aimed to restore tribal rights over their land and abolish exploitative practices like forced labor (**‘Beth Begari’**).
 
 
 
• **Birsa’s Ideology and Legacy:**
 
 
• He advocated for a return to tribal roots and the rejection of foreign religions, calling for the revival of **‘Sarhul’** and other traditional tribal practices.
 
• He envisioned an egalitarian society free from oppression and exploitation, emphasizing the need for self-rule by tribal communities.
 
• Birsa’s contribution is remembered annually on his birth anniversary, celebrated as **‘Birsa Munda Jayanti’**.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts about Birsa Munda:**
 
 
• Birsa Munda is the only tribal leader in India whose portrait hangs in the **Central Hall of the Indian Parliament**.
 
• His rebellion led to the passing of the **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908**, which prohibited the transfer of tribal lands to non-tribals.
 
• He died at a young age of **25 years** on **9 June 1900**, but his legacy continues to inspire tribal movements in India.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **Jharkhand state** was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 in recognition of tribal contributions, coinciding with Birsa Munda’s birth anniversary.
 
• Birsa’s life and legacy are part of the school curriculum in many Indian states to educate children about tribal heritage and resistance movements.
 
• Several institutions, including **Birsa Agricultural University** and **Birsa Institute of Technology**, are named in his honor.
